artifacts.synopsis: The SJC denied most specifications of a complaint filed by TE Herron and others against Central Indiana Presbytery's investigative and suspension procedures, but sustained the complaint on the point that Presbytery improperly denied Herron access to Presbytery minutes while under process. The decision includes extensive discussion of pre-trial BCO 43-1 complaints ('interlocutory appeals') and the proper scope of BCO 31-10 administrative suspensions.

artifacts.synopsis: John Thompson filed a BCO 43-1 complaint challenging his indictment while his judicial case was still in process before the Session. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order because objections to a trial court's actions must be raised by the defendant during the trial or by appeal after final judgment, not by a separate complaint during the pendency of process.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC found Marshall's complaint judicially out of order on two grounds: that objections raised during a pending judicial case should be reserved for appeal rather than complaint (BCO 32-14; 42-3), and that no complaint is allowable in a judicial case in which an appeal is pending (BCO 43-1). Three commissioners dissented, arguing BCO 32-14 did not apply before trial commenced and that BCO 43-1's exception is limited to pending appeals, not complaints filed before a trial occurs.

artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission heard an appeal by TE John Grady from his conviction and censure by Southwest Florida Presbytery. The Commission sustained three of seven error specifications but found only one materially prejudicial. Critically, the Commission found that Presbytery misapplied BCO 13-9.c by claiming power to direct the minister to resign and then censuring him for refusal to comply; the Commission vacated the censure and remanded for reconsideration of appropriate punishment while the administrative suspension under BCO 31-10 remained in effect.

artifacts.title: Paul W. Lee v. Korean Southwest
artifacts.synopsis: Appeal by TE Paul W. Lee against Korean Southwest Presbytery's judgment finding him guilty of disobeying citations, rejecting admonitions, and other charges. The Standing Judicial Commission found KSWP erred on all issues through procedural violations including improper admonishment of judicial commission members mid-trial, failure to record trial proceedings, denial of cross-examination rights, and improper censure. Case remanded for retrial or dismissal.

artifacts.synopsis: Beverly R. Smith appealed her conviction on four charges (factiousness, gossip/slander, breaking membership vows, and contumacy) by the session of Covenant Presbyterian Church, which was upheld by Southwest Presbytery. The SJC reversed the conviction, finding the documentary evidence insufficient to prove the charges and that the session committed multiple procedural errors including failure to produce witnesses, prejudice, and improper suspension from the sacraments before charges were disclosed.

artifacts.title: Shive v. Central Carolina
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC reversed the session's imposition of excommunication on Dr. Robert Shive for inappropriate conduct while counseling female patients, remanding instead for indefinite suspension from the Sacraments, finding insufficient evidence of contumacy or impenitence to justify the highest censure.
